items.title: 54271_Charlie Holmes oral history interview
items.q: In the band there was Buster Bailey, Charlie Shavers and myself in the front line, and there was John Kirby, there was Fuller, the drummer...no, Big Sid was the drummer... John Kirby, Big Sid and...

ctx.x: Were there any other drummers at the time that you thought were very good?

Oh yeah, a lot of drummers around. Big Sid... Oh, a lot of drummers around. Some of them made a big name, some of them didn't. But all of them made a living. Some of them didn't care to make big names. That's just not...not only drummers. I mean, any instrument you can name. They had all kind of instruments in New York City, and players and one-thing-or-another. Everybody didn't get a big break, or this-that-and-the-other.

Now, there's a man today like...name... Because you'd know him. But he's been around here for years, too. He's never been a big name on his own, but today he is. And this goes from way back. A marvelous trumpet player, one of the best in the business. And he just worked from this place to that place, to this band, the other band, the best of jobs, the best of bands or the worst of bands -- it didn't make no difference. It was work. And that's Doc Cheatham. Do you understand what I mean? He was always a sideman,…
